Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1732); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king:--David.
BiblicalUsage: Dabid is the Greek spelling of David's name as it stands in the older copies, where the letter is a beta where the common text has an upsilon. Matthew opens his gospel with the book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of Dabid, and Paul in Antioch says God raised up David to be their king. The name is David's, and the spelling is the only difference.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the spelling matters because it shows the gospel was copied by real hands in real places, and the same king stands behind every spelling. David is the king after God's own heart, and Jesus is his son.
